question: Which of the following excipients is NOT used as a dye in the preparation of pharmaceutical forms ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Iron oxide -> commonly used as a dye in pharmaceutical forms -> 95% confidence. CHAIN: Titanium dioxide -> commonly used as a dye in pharmaceutical forms -> 95% confidence. CHAIN: Ferrous ferrocyanides -> used as a dye in pharmaceutical forms -> 90% confidence. CHAIN: Maltol -> NOT commonly used as a dye in pharmaceutical forms -> 95%
analysis: Excipients are inactive substances used as carriers or stabilizers in pharmaceutical formulations. Iron oxide, titanium dioxide, and ferrous ferrocyanides are commonly used as dyes in pharmaceutical preparations. Maltol, on the other hand, is not typically used as a dye but rather as a flavoring agent or fragrance in pharmaceutical products.
